# aeneid-068 (IX.446–529) — drafter's notes

40 units; `make_units.py` runs clean (no LINE COUNT / TOO LONG / NEWLINE / ENDING warnings). `t` comes only from `A.cut`; no `sc`.
Paragraphs: 446, 450, 459, 473, 503, 525 (all `p: true`; each note opens "A new paragraph in Greenough.").
Speech marks: the mother's lament opens in the 481 unit (`“Hunc ego te…`) and closes in the 495–497 unit (`vitam.”`),
as Greenough prints them; `l` and `i` carry “ and ” on the same units. No other speech in the part.

## Misprint calls (rule 5b)

None. The print is clean in this stretch: no lower-case after a stop, no closing mark joined to the next word.

Kept as printed, doubtful:
- **9.501 `Illionei`** (double l). The name is from *Ilion* and is normally *Ilioneus* (the Latin Library has
  `Ilionei`). I could not check Greenough's spelling of the name elsewhere (1.120, 1.521, 7.212, 9.569 …) under this
  brief. If he prints *Ilione-* everywhere else, this is a dropped-in letter and a clear misprint under 5b; then only the
  opening of the 500–502 note changes ("The print has 'Illionei', a misprint for 'Ilionei', corrected here."). Scansion is
  unaffected (*Ī-* is long by nature). `l`/`i` use the English "Ilioneus" either way.

Other Greenough habits kept and noted, not misprints: `Siquid`, `siqua` (×2), `Capitoli`, `avolsa`, `volnera`, `divom`,
`adfari`, `adlabitur`, `Adcelerant`, `adsueti`, `adspirate`.

## Latin Library variants noted (sense changes)

456 `plenos spumanti`/`pleno spumantis`; 463–464 `cogit… suas`/`cogunt… suos`; 481 `illa`/`ille`; 486 `funera`/`funere`
(with Servius's archaic feminine `funera` also mentioned); 514 `iuvat`/`iuvet`; 529 omitted by the Latin Library.
501 `Illionei`/`Ilionei` mentioned (see above). Orthographic ones ignored.

## Bracketed line and half-lines

- 9.529 bracketed by Greenough as spurious, kept in `[ ]` in t, l and i; the 528–529 note says so (copied from 7.645).
- 9.467 and 9.520 are half-lines; both notes say so (467's note gives the "Virgil died before revising" context once).

## Advisory: none (decision and reasons)

No top-level `advisory`, consistent with aeneid-067 (QUESTIONS 61). The content: the heads of Nisus and Euryalus
paraded on spears (465–467) and seen by the Trojans "dripping with black gore" (471–472); the mother imagining his body
left to dogs and birds, limbs torn (485–491); a heavy stone crushing the Volscian tortoise (515–518). None is lingered on;
each is a line or two in Homer's idiom (the head on stakes is Hector's threat in Iliad 18; dogs and birds are the Iliad's
opening). Displaying an enemy's head is an act of war, not torture or sexual violence, and it is less graphic than the
killings in 067 that got no advisory. Giving one here and not there would be inconsistent; the general ruling for
battle violence in IX–XII is still the owner's (QUESTIONS 61). Nothing is bowdlerized: l, i and n give the heads, the
gore and the mother's imagined mutilation at the Latin's force.
Drop-in if wanted:
- lede: "After the night raid, the heads of the two dead young men are carried on spears before the Trojan walls
  (465–472), and Euryalus's mother grieves over the sight."
- more: "The display is told in a few lines; the mother's lament imagines her son's body left to dogs and birds. The
  text is given unaltered, and the translations and notes render what the Latin says at its own force."

## Scansion worries (scan-fixes are not my job; for the reviewer)

- **467** (UNRESOLVED): half-line. `Eūrўă | l(i) ēt Nī | sī` — Greek *eu* one syllable, elision *Euryal(i) et*.
- **520** (UNRESOLVED): half-line. `mīssĭlĭ | būs cēr | tānt`.
- **501** (COSTLY 3.5): the scanner's fit is wrong — it makes *Iuli* two syllables with consonantal I. Right:
  `Īlĭŏ | nēi mŏnĭ | t(u) ēt mūl | tūm lăcrĭ | māntĭs Ĭ | ūlī` — *-nei* one syllable (synizesis of the Greek genitive),
  *Iūlī* three syllables, *-tis* short before the vowel.
- **477** `femineo ululatu`: hiatus, no elision (as 4.667): `Ēvŏlăt | īnfē | līx ēt | fēmĭnĕ | ō ŭlŭ | lātū`. The
  scanner will likely elide; the 477–480 note says hiatus.
- **480** *dehinc* one syllable (synizesis): `tēlō | rūmquĕ mĕ | mōr cae | lūm deinc | quēstĭbŭs | īmplēt`.
- **481** `Hunc ego te, Euryale, aspicio? Tune illa senectae`: I scan with three elisions, *t(e) Euryale*,
  *Euryal(e) aspicio*, *Tun(e) illa*: `Hūnc ĕgŏ | t(e) Eūrўă | l(e) āspĭcĭ | ō Tū | n(e) īllă sĕ | nēctaē`. Check whether
  a hiatus at *te Euryale* is intended instead; the note lists the elisions.
- **521** *Etruscam* with short *E-* (`quāssābăt Ĕ | trūscām`), as the 8.503 issue.
- Usual blind spots: initial *Ae-* at 448 (*Aeneae*), 468 (*Aeneadae*); *Teucri* 510, 516; *Euryali/Euryale* 467,
  475, 481; *exsangui* 453 (*gu* = gw, then elision).
